Findings of active lateral patella maltracking, with edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad, and osseous stress response in the lateral body of the patella.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

Articular irregularity and signal heterogeneity of the patellar cartilage, and underlying marrow edema overall suggestive of severe chondromalacia patellae.

The anterior cruciate ligament is intact. The tibial aspect of the posterior cruciate ligament is relatively thickened with focal intermediate signal thickening suggestive of scar tissue, and suggestive of previously low-grade partial tear. No posterior tibial translation.

The anterior horn medial meniscus is slightly extruded 3 mm beyond the tibial plateau. No medial meniscal tear is identified. Mild chondrosis medial tibiofemoral compartment.

The lateral meniscus is intact without evidence of tear. Mild chondrosis lateral tibiofemoral compartment.

No significant knee joint effusion. No Baker's cyst.

Bone contusion anterior tibia, just lateral to the tibial tubercle. Mild prepatellar soft tissue swelling.

INTERPRETATION: 

- Findings suggestive of previous posterior cruciate ligament low-grade partial tear. No abnormal tibial translation.
- Severe chondromalacia patellae. Mild chondrosis within the medial and lateral tibiofemoral compartments.
- Bone contusion anterior tibia just lateral to the tibial tubercle.
